meta.calc.title: Am I being paid right? NY home care pay check
meta.calc.description: Free calculator for New York home care aides, home health aides and CDPAP caregivers. Checks one week of pay against the {year} minimum wage, wage parity, overtime and 24-hour shift rules. Nothing you enter is saved.
meta.calc.appDescription: Free calculator that compares one week of a New York home care worker's pay with the state minimum wage, wage parity, overtime, 24-hour shift rules and PPL's posted CDPAP rate.
meta.ogAlt: CarePayNY: Am I being paid right? Free pay check and CDPAP guide for home care workers in New York.
footer.disclaimer.html: Estimates, not legal advice. CarePayNY explains New York's home care pay rules as of {date} and can't account for every situation. Union contracts (such as 1199SEIU), shift differentials, holiday pay, paid time off and other benefits can change what you're owed. The New York State Department of Labor enforces the state's wage laws.
footer.independent: We're independent and not affiliated with the New York State Department of Health, the Department of Labor, PPL or Medicaid. Rules version {version}.
notice.translated.html: This page was translated from English with the help of AI. If they are different, the English page is correct. To report a mistake, email {email}.
guide.name: CDPAP guide
guide.pay.name: Home care pay guide
guide.independent: CarePayNY is independent. We are not part of PPL, the New York State Department of Health, the Department of Labor or Medicaid. This page gives general information, not legal advice.

flag.privateFloor: If a family hires you directly, we use the home care aide minimum ({hca}). New York's law sets this minimum for any worker whose main job is helping a person at home with daily activities, such as bathing, dressing or eating. It doesn't cover someone who works only now and then ("on a casual basis"). For that kind of work, the general minimum wage ({general}) applies.
flag.shiftsMissed: On {count} of your 24-hour shifts you didn't get the required breaks, so you must be paid for more than 13 hours on those shifts (up to all 24). We counted {hours} paid hours for your 24-hour shifts.
flag.shiftsOk: 24-hour shifts can be paid as 13 hours only if you actually got 8 hours for sleep (5 of them uninterrupted) and 3 hours of meal breaks. If you were woken up or worked through meals, change the answers above.
flag.rateShort: Your hourly rate ({rate}) is below the minimum of {min} that applies to you by {short} an hour.
flag.pplShort: PPL says its base pay for CDPAP is {ppl} an hour when the person you care for lives in {region} (since {date}). The rate you entered is {short} less than that.
flag.stubShort: Your pay stub shows {entered}, about {diff} less than we'd expect for these hours.
flag.wageParity.yes: Because your work is Medicaid-funded in {region}, your employer must give you at least {total} an hour in total pay and benefits. With your rate, that's {gap} an hour in benefits (like health insurance or paid time off) or extra cash. The Wage Parity notice from your employer shows how they meet it.
flag.wageParity.maybe: Because your work may be Medicaid-funded in {region}, your employer must give you at least {total} an hour in total pay and benefits. With your rate, that's {gap} an hour in benefits (like health insurance or paid time off) or extra cash. The Wage Parity notice from your employer shows how they meet it.

summary.title: Home care pay check (NY rules {version})
calc.info.1: Home care workers have a right to a pay notice and a Wage Parity notice from their agency.
calc.info.2.html: CDPAP caregivers: PPL@Home, at pplfirst.com, shows each timesheet and its status. Our CDPAP guide explains PPL's payment messages.
calc.info.3.html: Free legal help: The Legal Aid Society helps home care workers with unpaid wages.
calc.info.4.html: The New York State Department of Labor takes wage claims. It's free to file a wage claim.
calc.rules.minimum: Home care aide minimum wage: {nyc}/hr in NYC, Long Island and Westchester; {rest}/hr elsewhere.
calc.rules.wageParity: Wage parity (Medicaid work): at least {nycTotal}/hr total in NYC ({nycBenefit} benefit) and {liwTotal}/hr in Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester ({liwBenefit} benefit).
calc.rules.shifts: 24-hour shifts: may be paid as 13 hours only with 8 hours for sleep (5 uninterrupted) and 3 hours for meals. Otherwise those hours must be paid.
calc.rules.overtime: Overtime: 1.5× your rate after 40 hours a week (44 if a family employs you directly and you live in their home).
calc.rules.note: Some state pages still show the older wage parity benefit of $4.09 (NYC) and $3.22 (Long Island and Westchester). The 2023 state budget lowered those to $2.54 and $1.67 from 2024 as the base wage rose, so total pay per hour went up. This tool uses the current amounts.
